rules.title: Annual General Adjustment Cap to 5%
rules.requirement: The maximum Annual General Adjustment (AGA) is 5%. If the formula in the Rent Ordinance results in an AGA greater than 5%, the AGA approved by the Board for that year can be no more than 5%. This cap does not prevent a landlord who has banked unused AGAs from previous years from implementing a rent increase greater than 5% in order to raise the rent to the rent ceiling.
rules.citation: Measure BB, Berkeley Rent Ordinance, operative November 2024
rules.quoted_span: The maximum AGA is 5%. This means that, if the formula in the Rent Ordinance results in an AGA that is greater than 5%, the AGA approved by the Board for that year can be no more than 5%.
rules.coverage_conditions: Fully covered rental units in Berkeley as defined by Rent Ordinance
rules.exemptions: Rent increases using banked (unused) prior year AGAs are exempt from the 5% cap when raising rent to the rent ceiling
rules.sanctions: Subject to Rent Board enforcement and review of AGA setting

rules.title: Nonpayment of Rent Eviction Threshold
rules.requirement: A landlord may not evict a tenant for nonpayment of rent unless the tenant owes an amount of rental debt equal to or greater than one month of the Fair Market Rent (FMR) value for a unit of equivalent size in the Oakland-Fremont, CA HUD Metro FMR as determined by the US Department of Housing and Urban Development for the fiscal year in which the rent is demanded.

rules.coverage_conditions: Fully or partially covered rental units; eviction ground must be nonpayment of rent
rules.sanctions: Eviction action for debt below FMR threshold may be dismissed; landlord violation subject to Rent Board action

rules.title: Tenant Right to Organize
rules.requirement: Tenants who live on certain properties now have an enforceable right to create tenant associations and engage in organizing activities. Landlords and tenant associations are required to confer in good faith in an attempt to address any issues such as: landlord-tenant relations, rent increases, habitability concerns, and other issues of common interest. Tenants have an enforceable right to organize and may petition for a decrease in rent if this right is violated.
rules.citation: Measure BB, Berkeley Rent Ordinance, operative November 2024
rules.quoted_span: Tenants have an enforceable right to organize and may petition for a decrease in rent if this right is violated.
rules.coverage_conditions: Covered rental units; applies to tenants organizing in protected activity
rules.sanctions: Violation of tenant organizing rights permits tenant to petition for rent decrease; retaliation against organizing is prohibited

rule.title: Utility Charges Set at Lease Start
rule.requirement: Utility charges must be a set amount incorporated into the base rent at the start of a tenancy unless the utility is separately metered and the account is in the tenant's name as specified in the lease. For tenancies starting on or after February 6, 2024, a landlord may charge a tenant in a fully covered unit for utilities only if either: the cost of utilities are part of the base rent, or the utility service is separately-metered and the lease requires the tenant to place the utility in the tenant's name.

rule.title: Material Lease Breach Eviction Standards
rule.requirement: Material lease terms only include mutually agreed upon lease terms. The alleged violation must cause substantial, actual damage to the landlord. The landlord must demonstrate that the tenant's behavior was unreasonable. In any notice terminating a tenancy for a lease breach, the landlord must clearly describe the alleged breach and must demonstrate that the tenant's behavior was unreasonable, and may not evict tenants for lease breaches that do not cause the landlord any actual harm. The landlord's notice to the tenant to stop the violation must specify the lease term, and describe the violation and resulting harm in enough detail for a reasonable person to understand.
rule.citation: Measure BB, Berkeley Rent Ordinance, operative November 2024
rule.quoted_span: In any notice terminating a tenancy for a lease breach, the landlord must clearly describe the alleged breach. The landlord must demonstrate that the tenant's behavior was unreasonable, and may not evict tenants for lease breaches that do not cause the landlord any actual harm.
rule.coverage_conditions: Covered units where eviction is based on material lease breach
rule.conflict_note: Rent Board cannot advise whether alleged harm is sufficient or whether behavior is unreasonable; these are legal issues for court
rule.sanctions: Improperly noticed lease breach eviction may be challenged; Rent Board enforces notice requirements

rule.requirement: Any notice terminating a tenancy must contain a statement that advice about the notice is available from the Rent Board, the current phone number for the Rent Board's Housing counseling services, and the current address of the Rent Board's website. The landlord must file with the Rent Board a copy of any notice to terminate a tenancy, notice to quit, and summons and complaint no later than three business days after the tenant was served with the document.

rule.title: Notice of Tenant Rights - Requirement for New Tenancies
rule.requirement: For tenancies started on or after December 20, 2024, landlords must, within fifteen days of the start of the tenancy, give the tenant written notice containing the following information: The existence of and scope of the Rent Ordinance; the tenant's right to petition against certain rent increases, if applicable; whether the unit is exempt from rent control; and any other partial exemptions which may exist. If the property has an interior common area that all tenants have access to, the landlord must post the notice in the common area. Landlords must sign the affidavit included on all tenancy registration forms confirming that the tenant was provided the notice.

rule.title: Registration and Reporting of Government-Subsidized Units
rule.requirement: Government-owned or -subsidized rental units like Section 8 and Shelter + Care units are now fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance. Landlords of government-owned or -subsidized units must register them with the Rent Board as either fully or partially covered, and pay an annual registration fee. Whether a unit is fully or partially covered depends on unit type and if Federal law, State law, or administrative regulation exempts the unit from the rent control provisions of Berkeley's Rent Ordinance. Owners of partially covered units must now report new tenancies to the Rent Board within 15 days of the tenancy's start date. Owners must also update tenancy information annually during the registration billing cycle.
